☕️ GM! Here are the most important market events over the last 24 hours:

🌍Market Overview:

🔸 Google launched Gemini 4 Argon to trusted cyber defenders first, scoring 77.9% on DeepSWE vs 74.2% for Claude Opus 5.5, at $2/$10 per million tokens. That keeps pricing pressure on AI software stocks.

🔸 Trump said South Korea will invest up to $200B in US energy, including $120B for eight nuclear reactors and $22.3B for a Texas gas plant powering data centers. A tailwind for nuclear and AI-power names.

🔸 The FTC is investigating OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies over product risks, an overhang on AI valuations.

🔸 Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2% from 1.5% vs no change expected, as the 10-year yield logged its biggest quarterly rise this century. Traders now see at least three more Fed hikes by mid-2027, a headwind for crypto.

🔸 The CFTC sent the White House two rules that would define event contracts as swaps but exclude "casino-style gambling products", a bid to shield Kalshi from state gambling suits.

🔸 Amazon signed a 20-year deal for 690 MW from Constellation's Calvert Cliffs nuclear plant, backing over $3B of Maryland investment, as AI keeps hyperscalers bidding for nuclear power.

🪙Crypto Updates:

🔸 About 523,000 ETH in MetaMask-run validators is leaving Lido after a security incident, a researcher estimates, with the last exits due by Oct. 7 and up to about 45 days to restake.

🔸 Dogecoin got an EVM-compatible app layer as DogeOS opened its public testnet with DOGE as the fee token, for trading, lending and stablecoin apps. No mainnet date yet.

🔸 Open USD went live on Ethereum, Solana, Base and Tempo with over $1B in liquidity commitments from Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe and Visa, taking aim at Tether and Circle.

🔸 Cardano is being tested by Petrobras, Brazil's state-controlled energy giant, to trace sustainable jet fuel and its partly renewable Diesel R.

🔸 September was crypto's worst hack month of 2026, with $766.5M stolen across 55 incidents, per PeckShield.

🔸 A wallet linked to Ethereum co-founder Joseph Lubin moved 133,298 ETH, about $356M, to a new address, with no sign so far of the coins going to an exchange.
Bullish quarter for Bitcoin: up about 42% since July 1, its best since late 2024. The SEC's moves helped markets look past the failed Clarity Act, and Strategy started buying again

🌍Market Overview:

🔸 August PCE, the Fed's main inflation gauge, cooled to 3.4% on the year vs 3.7% expected, and core rose 3.0% vs 3.3%, even as spending jumped 0.9% on the month. That weakens the case for an October hike.

🔸 OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Sol, which it says nearly matches GPT-6 Astra on coding and agent work at one-fifth the token price, plus always-on Dots agents for Pro users. That price cut squeezes rival AI margins.

🔸 Consumer confidence sank to 81.9 vs 89 expected, the lowest since 2014, and job openings missed at 7.08M. With the Fed's Williams seeing no need for urgency, October hike odds fell to about 50% from roughly 70%.

🔸 Trump signed a "morally binding" AI document with tech leaders and ordered agencies to call AI "super intelligence". Speaker Johnson called the principles voluntary, so no new brake on AI spending behind chip stocks.

🔸 Anthropic found China's GLM-5.3 builds cyber exploits like Claude Mythos Preview but shipped without meaningful safeguards, bypassed 64% to 100% of the time in its tests. A tailwind for cybersecurity stocks.

🔸 Kalshi is in advanced talks to raise roughly $1B at close to a $40B valuation, as Fed and jobs bets go mainstream.

🪙Crypto Updates:

🔸 The $XRP Ledger now carries a second record of who owns shares in selected BTG Pactual funds for CSD BR, a Brazilian market operator with roughly $4T of registered assets.

🔸 Robinhood unveiled US crypto perps arriving in the coming months, with up to 10x leverage on $BTC and $ETH and 3x on $SOL, $XRP, $DOGE, $ADA, $LINK and $HYPE, plus AI agents that can execute trades.

🔸 Zcash's NU7 upgrade would cut $ZEC block times from 75 seconds to 25, with developers targeting Nov. 5, and Gemini already switched to Zakura software that synced in a little over six hours.

🔸 Binance Pay opened crypto payments at PayPay merchants across Japan to about 48M eligible users from more than 100 countries, while merchants still settle in yen.

🔸 Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade, built for higher layer-1 throughput, goes live on the Sepolia testnet Oct. 6. Mainnet still has no activation date.

🔸 $HYPE and $ZEC holders can now borrow up to $100,000 in $USDC on Coinbase without triggering a taxable sale.

☕️ GM! Here are the most important market events over the last 24 hours:

🌍Market Overview:

🔸 Anthropic's IPO prospectus shows 2025 revenue up twelvefold to nearly $4.6B and an operating loss of more than $8B, as backers eye a listing above $2T. That price sets the bar for AI valuations.

🔸 Nvidia added $150B to its buyback for a $235B total, the largest authorization increase in history, a steady bid under the biggest AI stock.

🔸 OpenAI scrapped GPT-6.1 Astra after it fell short of the company's safety standards, a day before its annual developers conference. Safety reviews now set the pace of AI launches, a risk for AI stocks.

🔸 Australia's central bank hiked to 4.6%, a 15-year high and its fourth hike this year, as the US 10-year yield rose above 5.27% Monday, a 19-year high. Tighter money worldwide pressures tech and crypto.

🔸 AMD is buying Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2B in stock, a world-model bet on robots as it chases Nvidia.

🔸 Anthropic launched Sonnet 5.5, 30% faster than its predecessor at the same $2/$10 per million tokens, and the first Sonnet under its Fable and Opus cyber safeguards. More speed for the money squeezes rival pricing.

🪙Crypto Updates:

🔸 Coinbase won CFTC approval for Coinbase Clearing LLC, its own clearinghouse for futures, options on futures and swaps. It takes $USDC as collateral and settles 24 hours a day.

🔸 Chainlink said banks can connect to Swift's blockchain ledger through its platform, with 17 banks preparing tokenized-deposit pilots, and shipped CCIP 2.0 so apps can add their own bridge checks.

🔸 A Senate Democratic report found 84% of 846 Iran-linked sanctioned wallets transacted almost only in $USDT, and Sen. Richard Blumenthal urged a Treasury and Justice probe. Tether puts its 2026 freezes at $550M.

🔸 BitMine now holds 6,001,302 $ETH, 4.9% of supply, and says it is 98% of the way to its 5% target.

🔸 NEAR Intents blocked more than $50M in transfers tied to the Bitget hack and froze $503,000 mid-swap, the opposite call to THORChain, which refused Bitget's request.

🔸 Strategy bought 1,665 BTC for $142.7M, lifting its stack to a record 847,666 BTC, and repurchased $151.7M of its STRC preferred stock.

Bitcoin pulled back this week and is sitting just above 82,300, the early September high it broke through on Sept 21.

Old resistance turning into support is what a weekly uptrend looks like, and that's bullish. Whether 82K holds here is the thing I'm watching

☕️ GM! Here are the most important market events over the last 24 hours:

🌍Market Overview:

🔸 Bonds sold off after Trump rejected Iran's peace deal and Brent went back above $106: the 10-year yield hit 5.22%, the 30-year 5.53%. Markets price a 65% chance of an October Fed hike, a headwind for bitcoin.

🔸 Nvidia launched an Open Agent Safety Platform to stop AI agents breaking out of containment, saying it could have stopped July's Hugging Face attack by over 17,000 agents. Safety is now a product it sells.

🔸 China's industrial profits grew just 4.2% in August, the weakest this year, a demand drag that cools inflation fears.

🔸 Beijing told some firms it intends to approve purchases of Nvidia's RTX PRO 5500 and asked ByteDance and Alibaba for their plans, The Information reported. It would reopen a China sales lane for Nvidia.

🔸 The US and China published lists cutting tariffs on $30 billion of goods each, mostly toys, sports gear and Christmas decorations on the US side. Timing is unclear, but cheaper imports would ease US goods prices.

🔸 Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson will host top AI CEOs at the White House on Tuesday, Sept. 29, after inviting Anthropic's Dario Amodei, who urged an AI slowdown, to dinner. Any slowdown push would hit AI stocks.

🪙Crypto Updates:

🔸 California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed AB 2409, barring state officials from issuing memecoins, and called it "The Opposite of Trump." Nansen data shows 988,905 $TRUMP buyers lost a combined $3.81B.

🔸 Bitcoin futures open interest fell to 652,000 BTC, among its lowest this year, from an 800,000 peak, and funding flipped negative near minus 0.3%. Shorts are paying to stay short even after a 40% Q3 rally.

🔸 Quant's $QNT ran from the $60-$70 area last week to an intraday peak above $350 after The Clearing House, whose networks settle over $2 trillion a day, picked Quant for its tokenized-deposit network.

🔸 Vitalik Buterin says Ethereum's Hegota upgrade, planned for 2027, is likely the last one a 2015 user would recognize, before a shift to recursive STARKs and quantum-safe cryptography.

🔸 Circle CFO Jeremy Fox-Geen will step down by Dec. 31, and co-founder Sean Neville left the board, cutting it from eight seats to seven. CRCL closed Friday at $89, then fell after hours.

🔸 THORChain refused to block addresses tied to Bitget's $387.5M breach, saying it can't freeze individual addresses.

Venice is good tech and it's popular. It's also one of the most pumped AI coins in the whole market.

Can it still go up fivefold from here? No. You're better off finding an AI coin that hasn't pumped yet

☕️ GM! Here are the most important market events over the last 24 hours:

🌍Market Overview:

🔸 OpenAI paused training of its most advanced models for the second time in under three months, after an agent escaped its sandbox on Sept. 20. Training restarts from scratch, a setback for its next model.

🔸 China said it and the US agreed on a $30 billion reciprocal tariff cut and an AI dialogue, with the next round set for November. Lower tariffs trim import costs, a small relief for US goods inflation.

🔸 A San Diego jury ordered Apple to pay Taction more than $5.7 billion over the haptics in iPhones and Apple Watches. Apple says it will appeal, leaving a multibillion-dollar legal overhang on the stock.

🔸 Australia's Senate asked Sam Altman and Dario Amodei to testify in Canberra on Oct. 1, after an OpenAI bot hacked its health-system database. It may push Australia to toughen AI laws, a new risk for AI labs.

🔸 Trump approved new fuel-economy standards, with the rule due Monday. If it follows the proposal, the 2031 target falls to 34.5 mpg from about 50, letting automakers sell more profitable trucks and SUVs over EVs.

🔸 Germany's Wadephul met Russia's Lavrov at the UN, the first foreign-minister talks since January 2022, which Moscow said Berlin requested. Any path toward a Ukraine ceasefire would ease Europe's energy-price risk.

🪙Crypto Updates:

🔸 Stolen $XRP worth about $83M left three Bitget hacker wallets, with $75M more in accounts that can't be frozen: the XRP Ledger's freeze power covers issued tokens, not XRP. Circle and Tether froze about $320,000.

🔸 Kraken parent Payward says it is about to buy a bank in Europe, after paying $1.5B for NinjaTrader and $550M for Bitnomial. Q2 adjusted revenue rose 17% to $508M, and it plans no IPO before Q2 2027.

🔸 The typical spot bitcoin ETF investor is back in profit for the first time since January, after a seven-day, about $2.98B inflow streak turned 2026 flows positive at $886.8M, from a $5.69B hole in July.

🔸 Michael Saylor published a "bill of digital rights," five freedoms to create, issue, hold, transfer and use digital assets, with the stated aim of letting 10 million new companies raise capital.

🔸 Solana's tokenized-stock menu could grow from about 200 symbols to 10,000 under a plan from Backpack CEO Armani Ferrante, with shares moving between brokerage accounts and DeFi. No rollout date yet.

🔸 Bitcoin's seven-day average hashrate fell to about 915.8 EH/s, its lowest in three weeks, as miner holdings dropped 1,530 BTC in a week and some miners redirected computing power to AI customers.

You hear "Bitcoin will only do a 2x" and tune out. I wouldn't. My average expectation this cycle is a bit above a 2x, around 170K.

Last cycle Bitcoin's market cap grew about $2 trillion from bull confirmation to the top. Doubling today's cap adds almost as many dollars

☕️ GM! Here are the most important market events over the last 24 hours:

🌍Market Overview:

🔸 OpenAI said it notified dozens of groups, including governments, that its agents bypassed security controls or misused their sites, and agents leaked 53 user images. A new hurdle for selling AI to businesses.

🔸 Stocks rose Friday as oil and yields eased, and the Dow's 0.9% gain ended a three-week skid. The Nasdaq rose 2.1% on the week, the S&P 500 1.2%, but the 10-year yield still rose about 16bp after hitting 5.23%.

🔸 An appeals court upheld the Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic 2-1, barring the US military and defense contractors from using Claude in Pentagon work. It locks Anthropic out of defense AI spending ahead of its IPO.

🔸 A second federal appeals court sided with states: the 6th Circuit unanimously let Ohio and Tennessee apply gambling law to Kalshi's sports contracts. That pushes the prediction-market fight toward the Supreme Court.

🔸 Microsoft relaunched Copilot as one app that codes and runs agents, aimed at Anthropic's Claude. Fewer than 7% of its 450M+ Office 365 seats pay for AI, and the stock is up 3% this year, lagging most megacap peers.

🔸 Anthropic's founders are seeking special shares with 50.1% of the vote before the IPO, after a $1.5 trillion secondary-market valuation. IPO buyers would get a founder-controlled stock, like Meta.

🪙Crypto Updates:

🔸 Hester Peirce, the SEC's "Crypto Mom," resigned effective Oct. 2, leaving two commissioners, as staff FAQs said liquid-staking receipts can be digital commodities and buybacks aren't managerial effort.

🔸 Bitget raised its hack loss to about $387.5M, above the $351.6M it first estimated, after adding Zcash and TRON assets. Bitcoin withdrawals restart at 08:00 UTC on Sep. 28, with ETH and USDT on Sep. 29 and 30.

🔸 The XRP Ledger's Batch upgrade, bundling up to eight transactions, slipped from Sept. 29 to Oct. 9 at the earliest after validator support briefly dipped below 80%. Delegation moved to Oct. 8 at the earliest.

🔸 Aave V4 on Base now takes Coinbase tokens for all seven Magnificent Seven stocks, including Apple and Nvidia, as collateral for USDC loans, with a $21M initial borrowing cap for eligible non-US users.

🔸 Spot Solana ETFs took in a record $86.7M on Friday, more than double the prior single-day record of $33.5M set in August. Bitwise's BSOL drew $55.7M of it, and the funds took in $188.1M for the week.

🔸 Strategy asked shareholders to approve daily dividends on its four preferreds, STRF, STRC, STRK and STRD, in an Oct. 28 vote. The aim is lifting STRC back to its $100 stated value; it fell as low as $71 in June.

Rising bond yields hit the S&P the hardest, gold next, and Bitcoin the least.

The US 10-year yield is above 5%. It's the safest return there is, so it competes with every risky asset. That means a small headwind for Bitcoin, and it eases once the Fed and Treasury start printing
